correctness.rationale: For r≥3 on G_r=K_{2,...,2} (r pairs), the Connes distance with adjacency Dirac matrix is the reciprocal of the minimum commutator operator norm among real f with f(x)−f(y)=1. Pair-stabilizer and swapped-pair sign averaging reduce antipodes to f=(1/2,−1/2) on one pair (norm sqrt(r−1)) and adjacent pairs to the four values (1/2,a,−1/2,−a). The latter commutator reduces to a 3×2 matrix with rows (1,a+1/2), (a+1/2,2a), (sqrt(r−2),2a sqrt(r−2)); the larger eigenvalue F_r(a) of its Gram matrix yields the exact distance. Since the derivative matrix has full column rank, F_r is strongly convex; endpoint derivative signs give unique a∈(−1/2,0). Gram leading diagonal A_r>r−1 except the nonzero off-diagonal endpoint, so d_adj<d_opp. Expansion a≈−3/(8r) gives gap ≈1/(8r^(3/2)). Independently computed full 2r×2r skew commutators vs reduced Gram for r=3,4,5,8,12,20 and rational a trial values, agreement to <10^−11. No claim for r=2 or weighted graphs.
